Thanks again for the time earlier, Diane — great discussion. Quick recap from our side and a recommended plan to validate model fit and safety for the triage assistant you demoed.

Key takeaways from today
- Primary goal: automate intake/triage for patient messages while preventing PHI leakage and ensuring conservative refusal behavior on policy-sensitive prompts.
- Volume: ~1.2M messages/year (estimate you shared).
- SLOs: median latency <250ms for single-turn generation; tail <800ms.

Initial model recommendations (for evaluation)
- rw-instruct-13b-q4 (fast, cost-effective baseline; good for structured output)
- rw-guardian-7b-ref (lower compute, tuned for refusal/safety behavior)
- open-compat-70b (higher quality for edge cases; benchmarked separately)

What we'll deliver this week
- Short eval suite with: factuality checks, refusal/safety tests, hallucination prompts, and the prompt set you provided.
- Benchmarks: throughput/latency and token-cost projection for each model variant.
- A safety brief summarizing refusal rates on sensitive prompt categories (PHI, legal advice, suicide/self-harm) and suggested guardrail prompts.

Attachments: I attached the draft eval report and the cleaned prompt set you gave us.
[Attachment: redwood-eval-report-v2.pdf (PDF, 2.3MB)]
[Attachment: acme-prompt-set-v1.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)]

Proposed next steps
1) Quick 45-minute follow-up next week to walk the eval results and decide which model(s) to pilot. Suggested window: Tue/Wed mornings.
2) Security questionnaire (we can pre-fill items related to inference telemetry and retention; see attached partially filled copy).
3) If fit looks good, agree on a pilot scope (2-week pilot, 50k messages, can run on Dedicated or Private depending on procurement).

Open questions I want to confirm before the next call
- Any regulatory constraints we should fold into the safety tests beyond HIPAA (e.g., state-level breach reporting cadence)?
- Are there any blacklisted terms/topics to always trigger safe refusal?

Thanks — I’ll wait for preferred times.

Jonas Weber

Diane — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers here and a pointer to the full pages in the attached report.

1) Refusal/safety differences- rw-guardian-7b-ref: trained with a lightweight refusal head and conservative decoding penalties that favor non-action. In our tests it refuses ~92% of direct PHI-exfiltration prompts and produces a brief refusal message with a redaction suggestion when the content is ambiguous.
- rw-instruct-13b-q4: higher base capability; more likely to attempt redaction and provide structured safe responses, but in ambiguous cases it requires guardrail prompts (examples included) to avoid partial disclosures.

2) Benchmarks and TCO- Yes — the benchmark spreadsheet in the report contains a tab with: projected token counts, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and estimated monthly cost for the volumes you gave us. Link to the internal benchmark page below.

3) Failure cases- The attached eval report flags ~14 failure examples across categories. Quick summary: hallucinations on medication names (2 cases), overly verbose legal-advice-style responses (3 cases), unsafe direct answers on hypothetical self-harm prompts when not prompted with clear refusal templates (4 cases). Each example has the prompt, model output, and our suggested prompt rewrite or guardrail.

Attachments included:
[Attachment: redwood-eval-report-v2.pdf (PDF, 2.3MB)]
[Attachment: acme-prompt-set-v1.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)]
[Attachment: security-questionnaire-filled.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

Action items I’ll take on before our follow-up
- Prepare a short demo of the four guardrail prompt templates in the report (redaction, safe-refusal, escalation-to-human, contact-matching).
- Add a dedicated sheet in the benchmark with cost sensitivity if we turn on higher-quality model variants for the 5% of messages flagged as "complex".

Can Marissa jump in on procurement steps and pilot contracting? Marissa — can you share a pilot cost model vs a committed Dedicated seat estimate?

Thanks — I’ll wait for times.

Jonas
